title: A Global Economic Recovery Built on Shaky Foundations
content: The latest update of the Brookings-FT TIGER survey reveals that global growth has stabilized, with both advanced and emerging market economies showing positive momentum. But amid persistent inflation and fiscal profligacy, policymakers will still be forced to push forward with structural reforms to unleash productivity growth.

title: The French Far Right Embraces Austerity
content: In a recent speech detailing her economic program, the French far-right leader Marine Le Pen offered what can only be described as a populist vision of fiscal consolidation. Whether she can make such a paradoxical formulation work will now determine her own future, and possibly that of Europe’s nationalist right.

title: Rating Africa on Its Own Terms
content: For decades, African countries' borrowing costs have been largely determined by major credit-rating agencies whose methods overlook key features of these economies' institutions and markets. The new Africa Credit Rating Agency could mark a turning point, challenging how the continent’s credit risk is graded and priced.

title: Development Finance Needs More Than One Currency
content: For many developing countries, renminbi-denominated loans offer a credible, increasingly accessible, and cost-effective alternative to borrowing in dollars. Now that the stability and predictability of US economic policies and institutions are in question, the Chinese currency is becoming more attractive.

title: Mélenchon Is Right About France’s Debt
content: When, in the name of moderation, centrists brand every sensible alternative to severe austerity as “nonsense,” they leave voters only one electable rebellion on offer, and the far right is happy to supply it. That is what is happening in France today.

title: Fukuyama, Thiel, and the Revenge of the Last Man
content: In his new memoir, Francis Fukuyama attempts to redeem his thesis about the end of history. But Peter Thiel’s ongoing quest to escape government oversight and wrest control of the future from democratic majorities makes a mockery of his argument all over again.

title: The Journalists’ Revolt Against AI Scraping
content: Big Tech’s oligopolistic dominance has prevented the news industry from developing a sustainable business model for the digital age—a crisis that AI is exacerbating. To preserve this important pillar of democracy, the Spanish-language publisher Editorial Perfil is suing OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement.

title: MAGA’s Self-Destructive Culture War
content: Polls suggest that MAGA fanaticism might not be playing so well outside US President Donald Trump’s loyal base. But if the Democrats want to retake one or both chambers of Congress, they should concentrate on the economy and not answer Republican extremism with a culture war of their own.

title: How to Break the German Malaise
content: For too long, Germany’s political and corporate elite coasted on the country’s postwar economic and political success story, avoiding difficult but necessary reforms that could have kept extremist populist parties at bay. Now that the barbarians are at the gates, mainstream elites must rethink everything.

title: Europe’s Place in the Global Redivision of Labor
content: While the US continues to lead in software, some high-tech sectors, and hydrocarbons, China is becoming increasingly competitive in many high-tech, capital-intensive sectors, not least those once dominated by Europe. The EU does have a relative advantage in this new economic order, if only its leaders would recognize it.

title: The World Has Passed Peak Trump
content: US President Donald Trump, previously the most powerful, unpredictable force on the international stage, has now passed the peak of his ability to disrupt the international order. With his approval ratings collapsing, foreign leaders whose tenures will extend beyond his own are starting to write him off.

title: Global Financial Reform that Centers African Women
content: While gender-equality objectives often fall by the wayside in times of upheaval, the current rupture in the multilateral order creates an opportunity to build a debt architecture that will deliver for the women of Africa. The first steps toward this goal can be taken at this month’s IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

title: How Africa Can Leverage the US-China Thaw
content: As dollar borrowing costs soar, Chinese rates are approaching record lows. This divergence, combined with the US-China thaw, creates an opportunity for African governments: partner with the US on gas and with China on solar and storage, and tap lower-cost Asian capital markets to finance investments in both.

title: Closing NATO’s Deterrence Gap
content: With Russian provocations against NATO member states growing more frequent, the alliance urgently needs to develop a credible doctrine of punitive deterrence to guide its response to acts of aggression that fall below the threshold of war. Mere territorial defense is not enough.

title: The India-Pakistan Cold War
content: The current stalemate between India and Pakistan should be viewed not as a pause between rounds of negotiation, but rather as part of a deliberate Indian strategy of disengagement. India will return to the negotiating table only after Pakistan dismantles, comprehensively and verifiably, its state-supported terrorist networks.

title: The Next Era of Reform Must Be About Capability
content: Economic development should no longer be measured solely by how much finance is mobilized or how much fiscal space is created. It must also be judged by whether countries emerge more capable of setting their own priorities, responding to challenges, and seizing new opportunities to shape their own future.

title: With AI, Sharing Is Caring
content: Although the public's distrust of Big Tech is understandable, given past experience, that is not a reason to starve AI models of the information and data they will need to be useful. If serving the public interest is the goal, everyone relying on the technology's output has a duty to provide high-quality input.

title: Why the US-China Trade Truce Matters
content: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump’s agreement to extend their trade truce reflects the fact that both sides have leverage over the other. In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, the current fragile equilibrium may be the best one can hope for.

title: Brazil’s Voters Have Moved
content: A strong performance by the right-wing, Donald Trump-aligned candidate in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election demonstrates that the left-wing ruling party has failed to keep up with the times. The Brazilian electorate is older, more devout, and more preoccupied with crime and personal security than it once was.

title: Does Inclusive Finance Really Need Stablecoins?
content: Today, 1.3 billion adults—more than half of them women—remain excluded from the formal financial system, and lower-income consumers still struggle to find and access the financial products and services they need. Contrary to much hype, stablecoins are not the best way to solve either of these problems.
